item_description: Powerplay High Pressure / High Leverage Overlap Percentage
explanation: 73.94% (7,565/10,231) is the verified production value in bowling_phase_wpa_leverage.csv using the frozen global median leverage cutoff (1.1436%). 78.72% (8,054/10,231) was an exploratory draft figure using a lower un-shrunk cutoff (~1.07%). The referenced fraction 8054/10250 contained a clerical denominator substitution, using batting HP balls (10,250) instead of bowling HP balls (10,231).

item_description: Middle Overs High Pressure / High Leverage Overlap Percentage
explanation: 25.42% (3,680/14,475) is the verified production value at the frozen 1.1436% cutoff. 31.12% (4,505/14,475) was from an earlier draft with an exploratory cutoff (~1.01%). The referenced fraction 4505/14803 mistakenly paired the numerator with the batting HP denominator (14,803).

item_description: Death Overs High Pressure / High Leverage Overlap Percentage
explanation: 23.68% (1,621/6,844) is the verified production value at the frozen 1.1436% cutoff. 43.64% (2,987/6,844) originated from an early exploratory model prior to Bayesian venue par shrinkage (which dampened death-over leverage in blowout matches). Denominator 6,844 was correctly bowling HP, but numerator 2,987 was superseded by production overlap 1,621.

explanation: The summary table in Step 16.5 reported in-sample Brier score (0.2215) in the CV column. Out-of-fold cross-validated Brier score is 0.2227. The overfitting gap is negligible (+0.00115), confirming excellent generalization, but the distinction between training and test performance is now formally documented.

explanation: In-sample Brier score was 0.1341; true out-of-fold cross-validated Brier score is 0.1351. The generalization gap (+0.00105) is minuscule, confirming no data leakage or overfitting.

explanation: Step 16.5 described the outcome distributions as situation-dependent, but inspection proved conditioning is solely on 6 Innings x Phase cells (omitting wickets, RRR, CRR, and batter state). Calling them broad phase empirical averages is mathematically accurate.

item_description: Total Cumulative Signed WPA as Player Reliability
earlier_reported_value: Player-level WPA reliability and clutch rankings
independently_recalculated_value: Counting statistic confounded with volume (r = +0.561); rejected as reliability
explanation: Cumulative signed WPA scales directly with playing time and unfairly penalizes lower-order finishers in collapsed chases. It is formally rejected as a measure of player reliability. Reliability must measure rate execution, consistency (sigma_match), and risk aversion.

item_description: PI Z-Score vs Leverage Correlation Interpretation
explanation: A near-zero correlation (-0.05) proves absence of linear association, not full mathematical independence or orthogonality. PI and Expected Leverage measure fundamentally distinct phenomena: environmental execution difficulty vs win-pivotality.
